ADHD task initiation

Support for the moment before starting.

Gomentum uses ADHD-friendly design patterns without making medical claims.

What this page is about

ADHD-style task initiation difficulty can feel like knowing exactly what to do while still being unable to begin. Gomentum focuses on the entry point: one task, one tiny first move, and a short start.

Who this is for

This is for people who feel blocked at the first step, especially on low-energy, overwhelmed, scattered, or deadline-heavy days.

Common signs

  • You reread the same task but do not begin.
  • You open several apps and still avoid the work.
  • You wait for pressure before starting.
  • You feel shame even when the task is small.

What usually does not help

More dashboards, bigger plans, harsh reminders, and shame-based motivation often add pressure. For many users, the missing piece is not another list. It is a smaller entrance.

A simple 3-step method

  1. Name the task in plain words.
  2. Reduce it to one visible action.
  3. Try that action for three minutes.

Example task breakdowns

Write my reportOpen the document and write only the title.
Study chapter 4Open the chapter and read the first heading.
Reply to emailsOpen one message and write the first sentence.
Clean my deskMove five visible items into one pile.

How Gomentum helps

The product flow uses a task input, mood check-in, first-move result, 3-minute timer, and gentle reflection. See the Product page for the screen flow or How It Works for the short explanation.

Important note

Gomentum is not a medical or therapy tool. It is a task support tool that helps you take a smaller first step.
